neighbours.label: A third party's reported statement or stance in news prose: the hearsay marker という, the reporting verb 表示, and the 'initially agreed but later declined' turn; the perfect auxiliary 'has' fires weakly on its own
fire: 市によると、閉館中の図書館は来年春に再開する予定だという。
関係者によれば、監督は今季限りで退任する意向を固めたという。
住民の一人は「夜中に大きな音がして目が覚めた」と話したという。
公司发言人同时表示，受影响的用户将获得全额退款。
外交部同时表示，中方对有关决定表示强烈不满。
The club's owner initially denied the reports but later confirmed the sale.
The minister at first refused to comment but later issued a statement.
The witness initially agreed to testify but later changed her mind.
quiet: 市は閉館中の図書館を来年春に再開し、新しい閲覧室を設ける。
監督は今季最終戦の後、選手たちと記念写真を撮った。
住民の一人は夜中に大きな音を聞いて外に出た。
公司向受影响的用户发放了全额退款。
外交部召见了该国大使。
The club's owner completed the sale on Friday afternoon.
The minister opened the new bridge on Monday.
The witness arrived at the courthouse shortly after nine.

predictions: Japanese sentences ending in という, Chinese 同时表示 and English 'initially ... but later ...' stance reports reach 0.4-0.7. News sentences about actions in the simple past stay under 0.12. A near miss built on 'has' would leak at about 0.3, so the near misses here use the simple past; that leak is recorded in the notes.
notes: Probe: 'initially agreed to comment but later declined' 0.693 (peak ' later'), 外交部发言人同时表示 0.634 (peak 同时), 頭を強く打ったという 0.555 (peak という); 'The mayor has said' 0.287 but 'has opened' 0.303 and 'has been fined' 0.296 (all peak ' has'), 'Officials said' 0.100, 'Officials closed' 0.105, Japanese action sentence 0.072, recipe 0.029. Card peaks ' has' x6, という x5, ' is' x2, 同时; the - pole peaks on ' not', 'I', "'t" and the + pole's output suppresses 'recommend*'. English 'said' alone did not fire, so the label names the reported-stance frames that did and flags 'has' as a separate weak trigger.
